# Semi-skimmed milk

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="semi-skimmed-milk-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="semi-skimmed-milk-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="semi-skimmed-milk-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Semi-skimmed milk in the HMI library has 35 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, Ba, CrIII, CrVI and Tl from 3 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury and nickel and others, in 35 results from 3 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Semi-skimmed milk, as sold from Microwaved had CrIII higher at 4.43 µg/kg, against 4.34 µg/kg for Hot plate in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>

<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Semi-skimmed milk overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Semi-skimmed milk in the HMI library has 35 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, Ba, CrIII, CrVI and Tl from 3 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in semi-skimmed milk, as sold from 1 result in 1 reporting region, with subgroup medians below 90 µg/kg, mostly non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Higher results came from contaminated or exposed settings rather than ordinary supply. Semi-skimmed milk, as sold from Raw had CrIII higher at 4.5 µg/kg, against 4.34 µg/kg for Hot plate in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the semi-skimmed milk came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.



<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as semi-skimmed milk

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers semi-skimmed milk, as sold (35 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Results stay on the basis each source reports: as sold or fresh weight, dry weight, or unstated. Dry-weight, as-sold and unstated results are never pooled, and no moisture conversion is applied.

Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Monitoring medians are HMI calculations from individual submissions; non-detects remain intervals between zero and the reporting limit and are never read as zero.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

0 rows can be rated against an HMI reference for the same form and basis, 12 rows have a direct same-study comparison, and the rest stay unrated with the reason recorded.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-semi-skimmed-milk" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-semi-skimmed-milk-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of semi-skimmed milk, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:semi-skimmed-milk-a1bf024ce5f4:8c023ba735ae"><summary>HMI semi-skimmed milk Pb reference · Semi-skimmed milk, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:semi-skimmed-milk-a1bf024ce5f4:8c023ba735ae"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI semi-skimmed milk Pb reference · Semi-skimmed milk, as sold. Semi-skimmed milk, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤90</td><td>≤90</td><td>≤90</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤90</td><td>≤90</td><td>≤90</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>1 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>1</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for semi-skimmed milk, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for semi-skimmed milk, as sold on this basis in the completed semi-skimmed milk ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach semi-skimmed milk

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach semi-skimmed milk comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Semi-skimmed milk, as sold from Raw had CrIII higher at 4.5 µg/kg, against 4.34 µg/kg for Hot plate in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

In one study, CrIII across 9 groups of semi-skimmed milk ranged from 0.48 µg/kg (retail product 4) to 1.93 µg/kg (retail product 10 (row printed 'Raw')); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing semi-skimmed milk for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>
<a id="which-methods-species-measurements-validation-evidence-and-reporting-limits-are-needed"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-027"></a>
<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 4 µg/kg (Baxter et al. 2015) to 90 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

A useful lot result names the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below the limit that applies.

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Semi-skimmed milk FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-semi-skimmed-milk" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-semi-skimmed-milk" data-question="What heavy metals are found in semi-skimmed milk?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in semi-skimmed milk?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, Ba, CrIII, CrVI and Tl in semi-skimmed milk, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in semi-skimmed milk, as sold from 1 result in 1 reporting region, with subgroup medians below 90 µg/kg, mostly non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-semi-skimmed-milk" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-semi-skimmed-milk" data-question="How do heavy metals get into semi-skimmed milk?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into semi-skimmed milk?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, semi-skimmed milk from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than semi-skimmed milk from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Semi-skimmed milk, as sold from Microwaved had CrIII higher at 4.43 µg/kg, against 4.34 µg/kg for Hot plate in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-semi-skimmed-milk-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-semi-skimmed-milk-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of semi-skimmed milk measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of semi-skimmed milk measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, CrIII across 9 groups of semi-skimmed milk ranged from 0.48 µg/kg (retail product 4) to 1.93 µg/kg (retail product 10 (row printed 'Raw')); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Saraiva M, Chekri R, Guérin T, Sloth JJ, Jitaru P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Chromium speciation analysis in raw and cooked milk and meat samples by species-specific isotope dilution and HPLC-ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants Part A 38(2):304-314</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/saraiva2021-chromium-speciation-milk-meat-cooking-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-semi-skimmed-milk-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-semi-skimmed-milk-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in semi-skimmed milk is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in semi-skimmed milk is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 1 result from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
